comments.author: geddy
comments.body:
I've really changed my opinions about AI in game development since.. I started working on some little side games with AI. The fact is, if the game feels good to play, it doesn't really matter how it was created. That's my thought on it anyway. I'll probably sound like a bot but I'm a software engineer by day and I use AI all the time for work. There's a difference between vibe-coding some junk and moving faster through the more laborious tasks so you can focus on the small parts that make the game actually fun to play.

If it enables random people to create new games or giant companies to create better ones, the bad ones will still get filtered out the same way they are now: crappy games don't get very far while good games while succeed. The development method is completely independent of the end result.
